title: Yara and the Cover
premise: Vesper Amberdale, a hostage negotiator haunted by the one call that ended in blood, receives a calendar invite from their handler — dead for three days. The meeting pulls them into a covert cell planning to stage a catastrophic 'accident' at an international summit, and the only person who can identify the inside man is Vesper's estranged protégé, Yara, who walked away after the failure they share. As rules are rewritten around them and every ally becomes a suspect, Vesper must choose between protocol and people, trading their badge, their record, and finally their own cover identity to expose the plot. In the end, the attack is stopped at the cost of Vesper's official existence — but Yara, carrying what she learned, becomes the negotiator Vesper could never be.
about_author: Paloma Sandoval is a former crisis-line counselor who spent six years listening to strangers talk themselves back from ledges before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who keep other people alive for a living, and lives in Lisbon with two rescue dogs who have never once followed her instructions.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Ten years after the Marlowe failure, Vesper works by-the-book negotiations until a calendar invite arrives from Handler Reyes — dead since Tuesday. Against every rule, they open it: coordinates, tomorrow's date, and Yara's name. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into compulsion; Vesper realizes someone wants them off the board entirely.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. At the coordinates — a decommissioned tram depot — Vesper finds no body, only a burner phone playing Reyes's last voicemail, cut mid-sentence. Security flags Vesper's unauthorized presence; Internal Affairs opens a file. Beat: isolation. Vesper understands they're being framed into the plot's margins, where deniable people go.

chapters.title: Yara
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Now a private security contractor guarding summit logistics, Yara spots Vesper surveilling the venue and confronts them with ten years of anger. Their argument cracks open the shared wound of Marlowe. Beat: reluctant alliance. Yara reveals an anomaly in the venue's fire-suppression retrofit — something scheduled to fail beautifully.

chapters.title: The Accident Schedule
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Following the retrofit contract up a shell-company chain, they find a timeline: a gas release timed to the summit's opening ceremony, engineered to read as infrastructure decay. Beat: rising dread. Every document they touch is logged; someone inside the negotiation unit is feeding the plotters Vesper's movements.

chapters.title: Inside Man
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Vesper runs an old negotiator's trick on their own colleagues, staging three conflicting briefings to see which version leaks. It works — and the leak is Director Hale, the mentor who taught Vesper every rule. Beat: betrayal. Hale offers Vesper a place in the new order, framing the attack as necessary reset.

chapters.title: What Marlowe Cost
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Yara finally tells her side of Marlowe: she followed Vesper's orders exactly, and has hated them for taking the blame alone. The confession reframes Vesper's decade of rigid rule-following as penance, not principle. Beat: catharsis. They stop negotiating with each other and start trusting — just as IA suspends Vesper.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Suspended, discredited, and with Hale's people closing in, Vesper goes dark using tradecraft Reyes left hidden in the voicemail's metadata — proof Reyes suspected Hale and died for it. Beat: transformation. Vesper sheds the rulebook deliberately for the first time, choosing people over protocol, and calls Yara in from outside.

chapters.title: The Longest Hour
chapters.summary: POV: alternating. Summit eve: Yara gets herself assigned to the venue's night shift while Vesper talks their way past Hale's cleaner team using nothing but voice and leverage. Beat: peak tension. They reach the suppression control room and find the release system armed on a countdown they cannot legally touch.

chapters.title: Cover Story
chapters.summary: POV: Vesper. Climax. Vesper negotiates with Hale directly over an open line, trading the one thing he wants — silence about his role — against the abort code, then burns the deal aloud so the summit's security detail hears everything. Hale's own people stand down; the countdown dies at ninety seconds. Beat: sacrifice and triumph entangled.

chapters.title: Off the Board
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. In the aftermath, Vesper's records are quietly erased — the price of the deal — leaving no negotiator named Vesper Amberdale anywhere. Yara finds them at the tram depot with a burner phone and no history. Beat: found family and inheritance. Yara takes Vesper's old badge number, and the board keeps a new name on it.
